reads.found: ⭐ A SECOND [sic:] CANDIDATE WITHDRAWN AT THE SECOND PRINTING. Gallica 1313D sets 'Obsecro vos, FATRES' -- a non-word, our TEI agreeing; the archive prints 'fratres', clean. No marker fired; crux carries both. DITTOGRAPHY CONFIRMED ON BOTH PRINTINGS at 1313A: 'reddentIS reddentES retributionem inimicis suis', two forms of the same participle with no punctuation between them (a speck above the second is dirt, not a mark). Marked [d:] on the FIRST copy per Pattern 11a: the sentence's frame is 'in Romanis exsultantibus, qui... venerunt', which needs the nominative plural reddentes; reddentis is the genitive of the Vulgate lemma vox Domini reddentis and is the eye-skip. One candidate REFUTED at the plate: 1314C 'my-/steria' is an ordinary line-break hyphenation, so our TEI's 'mysteria' is right. Pattern 8 confirmed twice: 1314A 'scripsere naturis' and 'per quem omnia operatur' both end with NO terminal stop on the plate; the English leaves both unstopped. Also on the plate: 1313B prints 'VERS. 10. -- Laetamini' with a normal em rule, so our TEI's 'VERS. 10.emdash;' is a mangled entity on OUR side (patch filed). [var:] fired: Rm 12:1 corda vestra for corpora vestra (1313D); Am 9:10 Gladio Dei peribunt for In gladio morientur, without populi mei (1314B); Is 34:5 et usque ad terram descendit for ecce super Idumaeam descendet (1314D). Foot of both columns blank on both printings.

reads.found: ⭐ A THIRD [sic:] CANDIDATE WITHDRAWN AT THE SECOND PRINTING. Gallica 1315A breaks the line after 'meridia' with NO hyphen and resumes 'nam, scilicet plagam', which reads as Pattern 10 split type; the archive prints 'meridia-' WITH the hyphen, so it is an ordinary line-break and the word is meridianam. No marker fired; our TEI's 'meridia nam' is a transcription loss (patch filed). CONFIRMED AS MIGNE'S at 1315A: the attribution reads '(HIER ]' -- open paren, no stop, closing SQUARE bracket -- where our TEI prints '(HIER.]'; the English carries the plate's form and the added stop is filed as a patch. LAST-PAGE CHECK: the work ends at 1316C with 'agentes gratias visa impiorum ineffabili poena.' There is NO colophon, subscription or EXPLICIT for the Glossa itself and no editor's closing note. Below a full-measure rule the page carries the tome's own table of contents, ORDO RERUM QUAE IN HOC TOMO CONTINENTUR (which is also the running head already printed at the top of this leaf), closing 'FINIS TOMI CENTESIMI DECIMI TERTII.' ⭐ THE TWO PRINTINGS DIVERGE IN THAT TABLE: Gallica prints 0000 against Liber Ecclesiastes, Canticum canticorum and Liber Ecclesiastici and 0090 against Liber Sapientiae -- unset placeholders -- where the archive prints 1115, 1125, 1183 and 1167. Prophetia Isaiae reads 1231 on both, which is this work's true opening column. The archive alone carries a printer's imprint under the FINIS line ('Imprimerie generale de Chatillon-sur-Seine. -- Jeanne Robert.'); the Gallica copy's foot below FINIS is blank. Band letters: cols 1315 and 1316 carry A, B and C only and no D, because the work ends two thirds of the way down -- a real absence, not a gap. FOOT OF BOTH COLUMNS BLANK ON BOTH PRINTINGS: no numbered Forte layer, no asterisk cross-reference layer, on the final page of the work as on every other.
